2. The back ground of the case is that the plaintiff-Opposite Party No.1 instituted Title Suit No. 561 of 198 in Fourth Court of Munsif, Dhaka seeking a Decree of Permanent Injunction against Defendant Nos. l, 2, 5 and 6 Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, Additional Land Acquisition Officer, Dhaka, Executive Engineer and Deputy-Executive Engineer. Railway Division, Dhaka restraining them permanently from evicting him from suit property described in Schedule to plaint measuring i.e. 0.34 acres property without payment of Compensation Money in L.A. Case No. 63 of 1959-1960, and, also, without allotment of Rehabilitation Plot. Suit was thereafter renumbered as Title Suit No. 25 of 1990 on transfer to Fourth Additional Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka. Case of the Plaintiff Opposite Party No.1, in short, is that he became rightful owner and possessor in respect of 0.17 +0.17 = 0.34 acres property by way of Two Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds dated 30.10.1948 and 29.10.1948 in C.S Plot No.1356 corresponding to S.A. Plot No. 401 and 4019. Plaintiff constructed houses on 0.34 acres of property and had have been residing there with family members and, also, on inducting some tenants and realising Rent from tenants and has been enjoying vacant land on producing vegetables and leaves. S.A. Record of Right had been prepared in the name of plaintiff. Plaintiff recently in the month of May, 198 came to that property of C.S. Plot No.I356 was acquired by Government for Bangladesh Railway in L.A. Case No.63 of 1959-1960. Plaintiff, also, became aware that Defendant Nos.1 and 2 has been in charge of Acquisition process and Defendant Nos.5 and 6 had been engaged for possession and maintenance of acquired property. Plaintiff 3-4 days before got knowledge that immediate after Eid-U1- Fiter, Defendant Nos.5 and 6 would carry on eviction Process to evict the possessors of acquired Property. Further Case of Plaintiff is that he is the rightful owner and possessor of Suit Property. Defendant Nos.1 and 2 did never cause any service of Notice upon Plaintiff and no Compensation Money had been given to Plaintiff and process of Requisition and Acquisition is not binding upon Plaintiff. It is stated that Defendant without payment of any Compensation Money and without Allotment of any Land/Property for suitable living in Rehabilitation area got no legal authority or right to evict Plaintiff from Suit Property. Defendant Nos.3 and 4 having been in permissive possession with permission of Plaintiff on a Portion of Suit Property had been made Defendant in the Shit. 

 3. Petitioner of the instant Civil Revision Case as Defendant Contested the Suit on filing Written Statement contending inter alia that Plaintiff got no locus Standi in filing the Suit and the Suit is boned under Section 14 A of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act 1948. Suit Property was acquired by Government in L.A. Case No. 63 of 1959496o on serving Notice and on payment of Compensation Money and property was given possession to Bangladesh Railway in 196o and since then Bangladesh Railway had been possessing and using Suit Property. It had been further contended that Plaintiffs father, Uncle and others whose land was acquired got Compensation Money and Plaintiff is not entitled to get Plot and story of Possession of Suit Property is false, and, as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. Defendant No-3, also, contested the suit by filing a separate Written Statement with Governments that her deceased husband on 24.9.1955 purchased o.09 acres property by way of Registered Sale Deed and became owner of the said purchased property. It has been further stated that Defendant No. 3 and her daughter as heirs became owners of the said o.09 acres property and constructed house and placed some tenants on the said property. Her husband during his life time received Compensation Money with objection and filed a petition to Government to allot Rehabilitation Plot. Defendant No-3, also, denied any Ownership and Possession of Government and Bangladesh Railway on Suit Property. 

 6. Learned Assistant Judge Fourth Additional Court Dhaka decided all the issues in favour of Plaintiff. In deciding issue No.1 Learned Assistant-Judge held that Plaintiff did not institute the Suit challenging the Requisition and Acquisition and Plaintiff filed the Suit for Decree of Permanent Injunction and there is clear provision for granting Decree of Permanent Injunction under section 54 of Specific Relief Act and, as such, there is no bar in proceeding with the Suit. Learned Assistant Judge rejected the plea taken by Defendant that Suit is barred under Section 14A (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948. Learned Assistant Judge held that there is no bar in proceeding with the Suit as framed. 

 7. In deciding Issue No.2 Learned Assistant Judge in considering the statements made in plaint and evidence of P.W.1 and D.W.1 came to hold that Plaintiff got the cause of action to file the Suit. 

 9. In deciding Issue Nos. 4 and 5 Learned Assistant Judge held that Plaintiff filed certified Copies of Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds dated 29.10.1948 and 30.10.1948 and Plaintiff proved those two Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds in accordance with Law. Learned Assistant Judge further held that in accordance with Section 60 of Registration Act Ownership of Property conveyed by Two Heba-Bil-Ewaz. Deeds dated 29.10.1948 and 30.10.1948 (Exhibit 2 and 2 (ha) respectively) vested upon Plaintiff. Learned Assistant Judge, also, held that Plaintiff filed State Acquisition khatian which has been exhibited as Exhibit ka (K) and presumption of Law is that S.A. Khatian having been prepared in the name of Plaintiff, Plaintiff was found in possession on Suit Property during the period of preparation S.A. Khatian. Learned Assistant-Judge, also, rendered decision that from evidence, both documentary and oral it became manifestly clear that Plaintiff by way of two Deeds dated 29.10.1948 and 30.10.1948 became owner and possessor of Suit Property. In rendering decision Learned Assistant Judge duly considered evidence of P.WS 1, 3 and 4 who are tenants under Plaintiff since the year 1967-1968 and Defendant side could not bring out any sort of contradiction in versions supplied by P.W.s. Learned Assistant Judge, also, came to hold that Defendant failed to prove that Notice of Requisition and Acquisition had been served upon Plaintiff. Learned Assistant Judge taking into account provision embodied in Section. 4 of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act 1948 and, also provisions contained in Section 7 of Act of 1948 and Section B and Sub-Section B and Section C and, also, relevant sections of Ordinance No. IX of 1969 held that Plaintiff having proved his ownership and possession on Suit Property is entitled to get reliefs prayed for. 

 12. Learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka being the Last and Final Court of facts on consideration of Pleadings, evidence and other materials or record held that Plaintiff on calling two volumes of Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds lawfully proved two registered Deeds dated 30.10.1948 and 29.10.1948 and two Deeds had been exhibited as Exhibit 2 and 2 (ka). Learned Additional District Judge, also, came to hold that witnesses for Plaintiff-Respondent gave evidence in support of possession of Plaintiff-Respondent over Suit Property and preparation of SA Khatian, Exhibit 1 having been prepared in the name of Plaintiff, possession of Plaintiff on Suit Property had been proved. Learned Additional District Judge also, held that Government could not prove its claim of Requisition of Suit Property in L.A. Case No. 63 of 1959-1960 but Plaintiff acquired Suit Property by way of Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds before one decade i.e. in the year 1948 before alleged Acquisition of Suit Property by Government, and, as such, Notice was required to be served upon Plaintiff at the time of Requisition and Acquisition in accordance with Law and Rules. Learned Additional District Judge further held that Defendant-Appellant did neither deny the existence of Deeds of Plaintiff nor did take any lawful steps in respect of the Deeds, and, as such, lawful effectiveness of the Deeds remains unaffected. Learned Additional District Judge on consideration of evidence of Abdus Salam, witness for Defendant who in his testimony dial not at all state that Government or Railway have been in possession of suit property rather he admitted that he could not say in whose possession suit property has been, and, on the other had witnesses for Plaintiff-Respondent gave evidence in support of Possession of Plaintiff on suit property. Learned Additional District Judge found that finding reached by Trial Court on the issue of cause of 'action of Suit and Limitation are correct and just. Leaned Additional District Judge in conclusion came to hold that in light of discussion made above it transpired that Plaintiff-Respondent had been in possession of suit property and a prima facie Title had been established by Oral and Documentary .evidence and Judgment and Decree passed in favour of Plaintiff Respondent by Trial Court having been in accordance with law and procedure those are liable to be maintained. 

 14. Statements made in Civil Revision Petition had been controverted by way of an Affidavit in Opposition/Counter Affidavit by Plaintiff Opposite Party No. 1. Plaintiff-Opposite Party No.1 in Affidavit-In-Opposition/Counter Affidavit, also, stated Points for and on behalf of .Plaintiff Respondent-Opposite Party No. l. 

 16. The learned counsel Mr. Shahed Alam appears on behalf of the, petitioner who has taken us to both the judgments and discussed the plaint case and also the case of the plaintiff-opposite party. The learned counsel argued that this plaintiff opposite party have no locus standi to file this suit and the suit is barred under section 14A of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 and the suit property has been acquired by the Government on serving notice and on payment of compensation money and the possession of the suit land has been given to Bangladesh Railway in 1960 and from that time the Railway Authority is possessing the suit property. His further case is that the plaintiff’s father uncle and others whose land has been acquired received the compensation money so plaintiff is not entitled to get any plot and the story of possession of the suit property is false, and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. The learned counsel further submits that the courts below failed to consider that the plaintiff did not challenge the acquisition on the ground of public purpose not they alleged any malafide on the part of the petitioner as such plaintiffs suit was barred by Section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948. As such the impugned judgment and decree of the Courts below have resulted in error occasioning to the failure of justice. He submits that the plaintiff in his deposition admitted that his father and uncles got the compensation money and that on 25.10.1960 he learnt that the suit land has been acquired but he did not make any complain. This shows that plaintiff had full knowledge of acquisition in 1960 and the service of notice on him is not necessary. But the courts below failed to consider this important aspect of the case, as such the impugned-judgment and decree has resulted in an error occasioning to the failure of justice. He further submits that in the fact and circumstances of the case the plaintiff has no right to get compensation, and in that view .of the matter the instant suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable and the court below should have dismissed the suit, hence the impugned judgment and decree has resulted an erroneous in the decision occasioning to the failure of justice. He lastly submits that the present suit is not maintainable against Railway, because after acquisition petitioner placed funds and then the land including the suit land was handed over to the Railway authority in 1960 and since then the land is in possession of the petitioner as such suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable, hence the judgment and decree of the court below are liable to be set aside. 

 17. On the other hand Mr. Md. Delwar Hossain, learned counsel in support of the judgment of both the courts below reiterates the present case which has already been discussed and the written statement and submits that defendant no.3 also contested the suit by filing a separate written statement where she contended that her husband on 24.9.1955 purchased .09 acres of land by way of Registered Sale deed and became owner of the said purchased property. It has been further stated that defendant no.3 and her daughter as heirs became owners of the said 0.09 acres land and constructed house and placed some tenants on the said property. Her husband during his life time received compensation with objection and filed a petition to Government to allot rehabilitation plot. Defendant no. 3, also, denied any ownership and possession of Government of Bangladesh Railway in the suit land. The learned counsel with reference to the judgment given by the trial court submits that the only Point which demands consideration in this Civil Revision is whether decisions rendered by Courts below warrant any interference by this Court in exercise of discretionary Civil Revisional Jurisdiction in Section 115 of The Code of Civil Procedure. 

 18. The Point now may be discussed and answered. Exhibit 2 and 2 (ka) are two registered Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds dated 29.10.1948 and 30.10.1948 with respect to suit property i.e. 0.17 acres + 0.17 acres = 0.34 acres from C.S. Plot No. 1356 corresponding to S.A. Plot No. 4017 and 4019 and those two Heba-Bil-Ewan Deeds had been lawfully proved by Plaintiff by calling volumes of Deeds Exhibit I. Slate Acquisition Khatian prepared in the name of Plaintiff and there is presumption of correctness of the Record of Right, that is, S.A. Khatian prepared in the name of Plaintiff and this Presumption is attached under section 144 A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It appears that Defendant-Petitioner did neither deny existence of two Heba-Bil-Ewan Deeds nor take any steps against the Deeds. Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. 1 in order to prove the Deeds examined himself as P.W.1 and put on witness box PW-2, Deed Writer of two Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds who proved two Hcba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds which had been exhibited as Exhibit 2 and 2 (ka) and, also, PW-5 and PW-6 who being employees of Office of District Registrar brought volumes of two Deeds. Plaintiff-Opposite Party examined PW-3 and PW-4 to prove his Possession on suit property. PW-3 stated in his evidence that Plaintiff is the Owner and Possessor of Suit Property and on suit property there are three "Pucca" Houses and Twelve Thatched Houses and a Shop and Plaintiff possessed those through tenants. PW-3 stated that he constructed Ration Shop on Suit Properly and he is a tenant under Plaintiff. PW-4 in his evidence stated that on the suit homestead he is a tenant in two rooms under Plaintiff and he has been in the homestead since the Year 1967-1968 and Plaintiff inducted many persons on suit property as tenants and in all there are 20-25 tenants on suit property under Plaintiff. PW-5 is Record Keeper of the Office of District Registrar, Dhaka and he came to Court with Volumes and he proved the Deed dated 30.10.1948 which was exhibited as Exhibit 2 (ka). PW-6 in his evidence stated that he carried Volumes from the office of District Registrar. Dhaka and proved Deed dated 29/10/1948 and the said Deed had been exhibited as Exhibit-2. Credibility of evidences of PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4, PW-5 and PW-6 could not be shattered by way of cross examination from the side of Defendant- Petitioner. 

 19. Defendant-Petitioner examined only One witness, DW-I. DWI Surveyor of L.A. Office, Dhaka stated in evidence that he did not know who stays in suit property. 

 DW-1 further stated that presently there are houses on suit property. 

 DW-1, thus, could not prove possession of Defendant-Petitioner on. In this context it can be conveniently said that in the event of taking of any possession on suit property by Defendant-Petitioner from Government by way of Acquisition of suit property and in the event of Defendant-Petitioner's actual physical possession on suit property, there could not be and cannot be any house/houses on suit property. From the evidence of DW-1 it became evidently clear that Defendant-Petitioner did not go into possession on suit property. On the other hand, Plaintiff opposite Party through his evidence as PW-1 evidence of PW-3 and PW 4 proved his exclusive possession on Suit Property. 

 20. Learned Assistant Judge as Trial Judge on due consideration of evidence of Plaintiff PW-1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4, PW-5 and PW-6 as well as DW-1 came to positive decision that Plaintiff on the basis of two Heba-Bil-Ewaz Deeds become owner of 0.34 acres property i.e. suit property and till to-day he has been in possession on suit property. Learned Additional District Judge as Last and Final Judge of fact, also, considered evidence of P.W.s and DW-1. Learned Additional District Judge found that witness for Defendant-Appellant (Petitioner) Abdus Salam D.W.1 in his evidence did not state that Government or Railway is in Possession on Suit Property rather stated that he cannot say in whose possession suit property is. Learned Additional District Judge held that on the other hand witnesses for Plaintiff-Respondent gave evidence in support of possession on suit property and proved Possession of Plaintiff Respondent on suit property. Learned Additional District Judge held that in a Suit for Permanent Injunction main issue is whether Plaintiff got exclusive Possession on suit property or not. Learned Additional District Judge ultimately came to positive decision that in the light of discussion it came to light that Plaintiff Respondent (Opposite-Party No.1) has been in possession on suit property and prima facie title had been established through oral and documentary evidence. 

 22. Law is well settled that concurrent decisions of Courts below specially decisions of Court of Appeal being Last and Final Court of fact cannot be interfered with unless it can be shown that finding is based on gross misreading of evidence or on non-consideration of material evidence or it has been founded on misconception or misapprehension of Law and misinterpretation of any material document or otherwise it is perverse being contrary to provisions of Law, evidence and materials on record. Support for the above proposition is sought to be drawn from a series of decisions, both of our and Foreign Jurisdictions: Durga Choudhurain Vs Jawahir Singh Cohudhuri, 17 Indian Appeal 122, Ramchandra Vs Ram Lingam, AIR 1963 SC 302, Abdul Mazid and others Vs Khalil Ahmed, PLD 1955 FC 38, Azizur Rahman Vs Per Vaizshan and others 1997 PSC 1329, Fazal Karim Vs Abdul Manafard and others 1997 PSC 1163, Federal Radid Commission Vs Nelson Brothers Board and Mortgage Company and others (1932) Vs National Relations Board (1942) 319 US 533, Guejt Heluering, Commissioner of International Revenue Vs Johan Kehoe, (1939) 309 US 267, State of New Yourk and others Vs United States of America (1946) 331 US 284, Fakhruddin Mia and another Vs Md. Khoda Baksh Sheikh, 29 DLR (SC) 268, Akrab Ali Vs Zahiruddin Kari 3o DLR (SC) 81, Abdul Matin Chowdhury Vs Chapala Rani Sen and others, 37 DLR (AD) 205, Naimuddin Sardar Vs Md. Abdul Kalam Biswas 41 DLR (AD) 3. Jasimuddin Kanchan Vs Md. Ali Ashraf 42 DLR (AD) 289, Mazhurul Borhan Vs AH Bhuiyan 1995 BLD (AD) 237, and Haider-un-nessa and another Vs Monowara Begum and others 1996 BLD (AD) 28o are some authorities for the aforesaid proposition. 

 25. Let me now address the point of Notice upon Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. 1 before Requisition and Acquisition of Suit Property by Government of Bangladesh for Defendant-Petitioner Bangladesh Railway. 

 Section 3 of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 speaks of Requisitioning of Properly required for Public Purpose or in Public Interest Section 4 of The Act of 1948 provides for Service of Order of Requisition which enjoins when an order of requisition has been made under section 3, it shall be served on the owner of the Property by delivering or tendering it to him, or, where the owner cannot be found, it shall be served by leaving an authentic copy thereof with some adult male member of the family of such Owner or, if no such adult male member of the family can be found, it may he served by affixing an authentic copy thereof to some conspicuous part of the premises in which he is known to have last resided or carried on business or personally worked for gain and also by affixing another such copy to some conspicuous part of the Requisition Property. An authentic copy of such order shall also be affixed on the notice board of the local Union Council and the order shall also be proclaimed by beat of drum in the locality in which the property is situate, Section-5 of The Act of i948 Deeds with Acquisition of Property Section enshrines: 

 (la) The Deputy Commissioner shall, if he considers that the acquisition of any requisitioned property is expedient for a public purpose or in public interest, cause a public notice to be given at convenient places on or near the requisitioned property stating that the property is proposed to be acquired. 

 (2) Such notice shall state particulars of the Property to be acquired, and shall require all persons interested in the property to appear personally or by agent before the Deputy Commissioner at a time and place therein mentioned (such time not being earlier than fifteen days after the date of publication of the notice) and to state the nature of their respective interests in the property, their objections (if any) to the acquisition of the Property and particulars of their claims to compensation for their respective interests. 

 Subject to the provisions of Sections 6 and 7 when a Property is requisitioned under Section 3 with a view to its permanent acquisition under Section 5, the owner of such property shall be offered, and if agreeable, paid in advance, before possession is taken over under sub-section (2) or section 4 a Compensation to the extent of 

 27. Plaintiff-Opposite Party No.1 on the basis of two Heba-Bil-Ewan Deeds dated 29.io.i948 and 3o.lo.i948 became rightful owner of suit 0.34 acres property. L.A. Case for Requisition and Acquisition of suit property along with other properties started in the year 1959 and L.A Case has been numbered as LA Case No. 63 of 1959-1960. Plaintiff Opposite Party No. 1 became Owner of Suit Property a decade ago before, initiation of Proceeding of LA Case to put it differently, right title and interest vested absolutely with Plaintiff-Opposite Party No.1 a decade ago from the date period of L.A. Case Proceeding Notice tinder Section 4 in respect of Requisition and Notice under Section 5 in respect of Acquisition of Suit Property was imperatively required to be served upon Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. 1. Defendant-Petitioner Railway could not produce any paper and document showing that Notice as mandated in Section 4 and section 5 of The Act of 1948 had been served upon Plaintiff-Opposite Party. It is in the evidence of DW 1 that no Notice had been given/served upon Plaintiff. 

 It is thus, manifestly clear that Plaintiff Opposite Party No. 1 though became rightful owner and possessor of suit property about Twelve (12) years back of the initiation of Land Acquisition Proceeding in LA case No.63 of 1959-1960. Notice as required to be served upon Plaintiff Opposite Party No.1 as mandated in section 4 and 5 of The Act of 1948 had not been served upon Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. l. It has been earlier held that possession of suit property till now remains with Plaintiff. No. Compensation. Money in respect of alleged acquired suit property had been, also, paid to Plaintiff-Opposite Party No.1 which is evident from the evidence of DW 1 who stated that no Compensation Money had been paid to Sujaruddin (Plaintiff). 

 Learned Assistant Judge took into stock provision contained in Section 4, 5, 5B and Section 7 of The Act of 1948 and came to held that Defendant failed to show that Notice of Requisition and Acquisition had been served upon Plaintiff. 

 28. Learned Additional District Judge, also, came to held that Notice in accordance with Law and Rules was required to be served upon Plaintiff-Respondent (Opposite Party No.1) in respect of Requisition and Acquisition of Suit Property and according to admission of Defendant Appellant no Notice had been served upon Plaintiff-Respondent (Opposite Party No.1) 

 29. Both Learned Assistant Judge and Additional District Judge concurrently held that Notice of Requisition of Acquisition of suit property had not been served upon Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. 1 and the findings of Non Service of Notice in respect of Requisition and Acquisition of suit property-upon Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. 1 had been concluded by concurrent finding of fact. I find no reason and ground to come to any disagreement with concurrent findings of fact of Non Service of Notice upon Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. 1 in respect of Requisition and Acquisition of suit property. From evidence of PWs and DW I and materials brought on record I am of this positive view that since Mandatory Provision contained in Sections 4, 5, 5B and 7 of The Act of 1948 had not been at all complied with, Requisition and Acquisition Proceeding in LA case No. 63 of 1959-196o and Requisition and Acquisition of suit property is absolutely illegal, void, without Jurisdiction and not at all binding upon Plaintiff-Opposite Party No. l. 

 30. On a plain reading of Provision contained in Section 14A of The Act of 1948 it is manifestly clear that Civil Court shall not entertain any Suit or application against any Order passed or any action taken under the Act and all Suits and Appeals pending in any such Court against any order passed or any action taken under the Act shall abate with effect from coming into force of (Emergency) Requisition of Property (Amendment) Ordinance, 1963. Since Plaintiff-Opposite Party No.1 did not challenge any order passed or any action taken under The Act of 1948. Plaintiff filed the Suit for Decree of Permanent Injunction under Section 54 of The Specific Relief Act. The Plea taken from the side of Defendant-Petitioner that the Suit is hit under Section 14A of The Act of 1948 is not tenable in law, and as such, the plea stand rejected. In this context it can be conveniently said that even if Jurisdiction of Civil Court is excluded, still Civil Court got the Jurisdiction to examine into cases where the provision of The Act have not been complied with or the Statutory Tribunal has not acted in conformity with Fundamental Principles of Judicial Procedure. Support for the proposition is sought is drawn from a series of Judicial Authorities of Superior Courts of The Sub-continent. Basic Judicial Authority is -Secretary of State vs. Mask and Co. AIR 1940 PC 1055= 44 CWN 709 P.C.
